title: Integration: From Atoms to Galaxies
objective: After this level you can connect nuclear fusion, stellar lives and galaxy formation into one story.
summary: Big Bang gas became stars; stars forged heavier elements and scattered them; that enriched gas became new stars, planets and you.

cards.headline: The atoms in your body have been on a 13.8-billion-year journey.
cards.body: Levels 91 to 93 made the universe’s first ingredients and its first stars. Now follow those ingredients all the way to you.

cards.headline: From the Big Bang to you

events.label: Hydrogen, helium and a trace of lithium form
Generations of stars forge heavier elements and scatter them into space
The Sun and planets form from that enriched gas

cards.headline: The great cycle
cards.body: Think of the galaxy as a kitchen that never throws out leftovers. Stars fuse light elements into heavier ones, just as the Sun turns hydrogen into helium. Massive stars end in supernovae that blast those elements out, scattering them into space. New stars and planets form from that enriched gas, and the cycle repeats. Every generation of stars cooks with what the last one left behind.

cards.fact: You are made of star stuff.
cards.context: The calcium in your bones and the iron in your blood were made inside stars that lived and died before the Sun formed. So your skeleton is older than the Sun. Well, its calcium is.

cards.headline: The cosmic cycle: connected
learned: The Big Bang made hydrogen and helium
Dying stars scatter them into space
New stars, planets and people form from them

questions.prompt: Which elements did the Big Bang itself produce?

options.label: Hydrogen, helium and a trace of lithium
Carbon, oxygen and iron
options.rationale: Those were forged later, in stars.

options.label: Every element in the periodic table
Only iron and gold
options.rationale: Those need stars and stellar explosions.

questions.explanation: The Big Bang made only the lightest elements; stars made nearly all the rest.

questions.prompt: Follow the ingredients from the Big Bang to you. Put these in order, from earliest to latest.
items: Hydrogen, helium and a trace of lithium
questions.explanation: Hydrogen, helium and a trace of lithium formed in the first few minutes. The first stars lit up a few hundred million years later, stars forged heavier elements over billions of years, and the Sun and planets formed 4.6 billion years ago.

questions.prompt: The iron in your blood was made inside stars. How did it reach the cloud that formed the solar system?

options.label: It formed in the Big Bang
options.rationale: The Big Bang made only the lightest elements.

options.label: Dying stars scattered it into space
Earth’s core made it from hydrogen
Comets carried it from other galaxies
options.rationale: It came from stars in our own galaxy.

questions.explanation: Massive stars forged heavy elements and scattered them in supernovae; the solar system formed from that enriched gas.
